(Main Game 2) Shin is accused by Reiko as being a good candidate, who should be selected to die. He immediately retorts that he is fine with this, and claims the role of the sacrifice. He had meeten up with Q-Taro, who offered him tokens in exchange for the laptop. Tokens can be used by players in the 2nd Main Game to trade cards, getting rid of roles such as the sacrifice or stealing a role such as the keymaster. Shin is hesitant since Q-Taro could be tricking him, but Q-Taro slides him is tablet under the door to Shin’s room. The tablet’s can’t be faked, so Shin made sure Q-Taro gave him undeniable proof: showing Shin that he was the sacrifice,  before considering allying with him. On top of this, Shin had seen Q-Taro placing the cards earlier, and so he had blackmail on Q-Taro as doing something like this implicates him as someone working with the game makers. There is a series of trades that occur, 5 in total. This meeting happens after the 2nd trade, where Q-Taro had obtained the sacrifice. Obtaining 100 tokens from Q-Taro, this gave Shin 2 free trades, as each cost 50. In the third trade, he swapped the sacrifice to Sara, understanding her personality well enough to know that she wouldn’t give the sacrifice card away as it’d be equivalent to murder. This is especially true because Joe, her best friend, died to the sacrifice cards rule. Everyone is surprised, because Shin swapped the cards of two players that were not himself. This was never said to be a feature, however Shin had come up with the idea himself with creativity. As Sara reveals she is a commoner by the end of all the trading once she is not one of the 4 elected for the final vote, Shin claims that Keiji, her closest friend at present, took the sacrifice from her, seeing as Sara couldn’t make any trades because she was accounted for and didn’t use the box. He accused Keiji and Sara of being accomplices, and that Keiji, one of the four people elected for death, will try and win the game via the rules of the sacrifice; taking out everyone except for him and Sara when he wins the vote. Himself, Kanna and Nao are the trio who can be reasonably voted to die in this scenario, so he suggests that Kanna should die since she is the least useful member of the group. When it seems that Shin has figured out Keiji and Sara’s collusion, Keiji reveals he is really the keymaster. Despite Q-Taro claiming it, Keiji does so anyway. Instead of Q-Taro counter claiming the keymaster role, Q-Taro instead claims the Sage role and uses the cards ability to back Keiji up. Confused, Shin questions them to which it is revealed that Q-Taro and Keiji have been working together to beat Shin, and that Keiji in the fourth trade, gave his Sage to Q-Taro for the keymaster. He knew Q-Taro was the keymaster because of the sage’s ability, which he used before making the trade. Shin had doubled back on his claim of being the Sacrifice once the 2nd vote began, claiming to be a commoner. Keiji brags to Shin that because of this information, it’s Shin’s time to die as being a commoner means he will be voted to die. Shin reasons that if the 1st trade was Keiji giving Sara the keymaster in exchange for a commoner, then with the other trades, there is no way anyone could have swapped and given Keiji the sage for this theory to work. He’d have to have been a commoner. Keiji debunks this counter argument, stating that he actually started with the Sage, and that the reason he could give Sara the keymaster was because as the sage, he knew who had it and could steal it from them, trading it for Sara’s commoner. Shin begins having an intense mental breakdown, knowing he’ll die. When it seems as though Shin is dead and will be voted to die, he reveals the truth, dropping the act instantly. The tablets that show roles are activated by fingerprints. Shin had already admitted he knocked Q-Taro out with a taser earlier. While Q-Taro was unconscious, Shin had observed his tablet, using Q-Taro’s sage ability to discover that Keiji was the key master. This entire strategy to defeat Shin, hadn’t worked, as before the 5th and final trade, Shin knew everyone’s roles thanks to using the unconscious Q-Taro’s sage ability. Shin had predicted and anticipated every step taken by the two from the moment Q-Taro showed up at his door, and had made his own plan. Kanna, the one he wanted to vote for the most, is actually his sister. She doesn’t even know, but he does and wants her to live. She is the sacrifice, and wins by being voted the most. Sara had the sacrifice after the 4th trade, and Shin correctly predicted that Kanna would steal it from Sara to die in her place because she loved her like an older sister. Keiji is the key master, Shin’s role is very ambiguous given he knew everything about everyone’s role before the final role trade which would have allowed him to take the sacrifice, or not take it, and Nao was spotted searching for tokens, which she’d only need to make the final trade. Under this logic, Nao should be the sacrifice and Kanna is a commoner. However, what the rest of the group bar Shin does not know is that Kanna will die for Sara, and so she willingly took the card. Due to this lack of knowledge and the evidence on Nao, Shin’s plan is perfect and that Kanna will be voted to die since the group believe Nao is the real sacrifice, because why would someone take it intentionally? This plan only fails because of Kanna admitting to being the sacrifice out of the good of her heart, and the game makers cheating to give Nao the sacrifice instead. If the game makers hadn’t interfered and Kanna hadn’t admitted to it out of her own kindness, then Kanna would have won through the sacrifice’s win condition, all thanks to Shin.
>= FRI, Planning Preparation, Planning Execution, Contingency, few limitations, Deception, Creative Thinking, Seeing Through people, Emotional Understanding, Acting Skills.
